kpis.statement: The programme serves 250,632 enrolled learners across 3 programmes.
83.6% of learners have been mainstreamed into formal school (209,614 of 250,632).
Across 2,800 evaluated centres the mean M&E score is 3.35 (of 4).

wins.statement: Catchup has mainstreamed 98.3% of its learners (188,223 of 191,555).

issues.statement: In ABAL, the leading dropout reason is Poverty (17,291 learners, 56.6% of ABAL dropouts).
In Catchup, the leading dropout reason is Poverty (46,755 learners, 51.5% of Catchup dropouts).
Innovation has mainstreamed 9.9% of its learners (385 of 3,877).
In Innovation, the leading dropout reason is Others (112 learners, 47.7% of Innovation dropouts).
336 learners have "Bad" nutrition status (0.2% of assessed).
Catchup: among learners with an attendance record, attendance averages 86.5%, but only 1.5% of learners have any record.
Innovation: among learners with an attendance record, attendance averages 97%, but only 1.8% of learners have any record.
Attendance coverage network-wide is only 16.8% — most rows are recorded as 0, and whether 0 means "no record" or "never attended" is unresolved.

actions.statement: Innovation's 9.9% mainstreaming rate is far below the network's 83.6% — investigate whether this cohort is early in its cycle or genuinely stalling.
ABAL's weakest subject is Life Skills, averaging 3.4.
Catchup's weakest subject is Life Skills, averaging 1.9.
Innovation's weakest subject is Life Skills, averaging 7.1.
56 centres score Poor (below 2 of 4), 287 Fair, and 2,457 Good — the Poor centres are where field support should go first.
The weakest centre-quality dimension network-wide is assessments, averaging 3.08 of 4.
15 centres are flagged for the lowest attendance and need a visit.

dataQuality.statement: Catchup: among learners with an attendance record, attendance averages 86.5%, but only 1.5% of learners have any record.
Innovation: among learners with an attendance record, attendance averages 97%, but only 1.8% of learners have any record.
Assessment cycle marks are barely recorded: baseline coverage is 64% but Cycle-1 coverage is only 5.5%, so subject averages mostly reflect the baseline, not progress.
Rangpur has only 8 learners — too few to compare against the large divisions.
Sylhet has only 3 learners — too few to compare against the large divisions.
Attendance coverage network-wide is only 16.8% — most rows are recorded as 0, and whether 0 means "no record" or "never attended" is unresolved.
Attendance cannot be joined to a learner: profiles/assessment use a 12-digit Student ID while attendance uses a different key, so per-student attendance and risk scoring are not yet computable.
